figures.title: Study design and optimizer placement
figures.caption: The same light network is trained under four update designs. Rows are reserved before fitting; confirmation does not refit models or thresholds. Top arrows show workflow order, not rows migrating between cohorts. The lower arrows describe simulated computation, not physical networking.

figures.title: Primary quality and false alerts
figures.caption: Each small marker is one training seed; the black diamond is the mean. No confidence interval is implied. All thresholds were fixed on development at the 5% target; actual confirmation false alerts may exceed 5%.

figures.title: Correct category recall for all eight classes
figures.caption: Cells are equal-weight mean recalls across seeds at the primary target, using the same confirmation cohort. Supports are per model, not tripled. The common 0-100% color scale prevents rare-class performance from appearing stronger than it is.

figures.title: Where each true class is predicted
figures.caption: Each matrix averages three row-normalized seed matrices. All methods share supports and a 0-100% color scale. Rows are true labels and columns are predictions. Blank cells are exact zero; nonzero entries below 0.5% display <0.5.

figures.title: Detecting an attack is not identifying its category
figures.caption: For each rare class, the three outcomes exhaust its rows: correct category, another attack category, or benign (missed attack). Percentages are averaged across three models, not independent replicated datasets.

figures.title: Quality gains retain communication costs
figures.caption: Left: primary mean macro-F1 and sample SD against counted application payload on a logarithmic horizontal axis. The dashed line is centralized-light quality, not zero centralized data-transfer cost. Right: synchronization counts. Payload is not measured traffic or latency; baseline raw accounting excludes initialization and message metadata.

figures.title: Four frozen operating points
figures.caption: Each point is the mean actual confirmation false-alert rate and mean macro-F1 at a predeclared calibration target (1%, 5%, 10%, 20%). Lines only connect those four measured points; this is not an ROC curve or threshold sweep. Large rings identify the primary 5% target.

figures.title: Earlier official39 baseline in its own evaluation
figures.caption: These are prior final-test results for the full39 references, with 2M training rows and argmax decisions. They are not directly comparable to the later 500k-fit, alarm-calibrated confirmation results. Seed markers and means are shown separately; no new test inference was run.

figures.title: Class imbalance in fitting and confirmation
figures.caption: The horizontal axis is logarithmic; bar lengths must not be read as linear proportions. Counts are frozen cohort metadata. Confirmation supports describe one shared population, not three times as many independent observations.

curve_policy: No invented convergence traces; only saved endpoints and four frozen alarm targets
